Twitch Bits to USD Calculator

A Twitch Bit is two different numbers depending on which side you're on. A viewer buying Bits pays Twitch's bundle price; the streamer who receives a cheer is paid a flat $0.01 per Bit. This calculator shows both sides and finds the cheapest bundle mix.

Why there are two numbers

Twitch sells Bits in fixed packs (100 / 500 / 1,500 / 5,000 / 10,000 / 25,000). The price per Bit drops as the pack grows (from $0.014 to $0.01232 at the US web base rate). The streamer always receives $0.01 per Bit cheered — there is no partner-tier split for Bits, unlike subscriptions.

Cheapest pack solver

For an arbitrary amount, buying the largest packs first is cheapest. Example: 6,500 Bits at 100-pack pricing costs $91.00; the cheapest mix (one 5,000 + three 500) costs $85.40 — the solver above does this for any amount. Mobile in-app purchases add roughly 30% for Apple/Google commissions.

Bits vs subs for the streamer

Per dollar the viewer spends, Bits are the more efficient gift: about 71% reaches the streamer, versus 50% for a standard-split sub. But subs recur monthly — a Tier 1 sub pays $2.50/month until it lapses. Most streamers treat subs as the predictable floor and Bits as the volatile upside (typically 20–40% on top).

Frequently asked questions

How much is 1,000 bits on Twitch?

Exactly $10.00 to the streamer. Viewers pay about $14.00 to buy them.

Do streamers keep 100% of Bits?

At the cheer stage yes — $0.01 per Bit goes to the streamer. Twitch takes its margin when the viewer buys.

How many Bits can be cheered at once?

Up to 100,000 Bits ($1,000 to the streamer) in a single cheer.
